quote: And, in the dawn, armed with an ardent patience, we shall enter magnificent cities.
source: Arthur Rimbaud, A Season in Hell, Farewell, the second to last paragraph (trans. Louise Varèse, 1961)

evidence.where: archive.org full text of the New Directions paperbook A Season in Hell and The Drunken Boat, translated by Louise Varèse (copyright 1945, 1952, 1961; NDP97 1961, reissued 2011); confirmed by archive.org full-text hits in The Art and Craft of Poetry (1981) and God at the Edge (2000) with identical wording
evidence.edition: Louise Varèse, A Season in Hell and The Drunken Boat, New Directions, 1961 (revising the 1945 translation)
evidence.locator: Farewell, the paragraph beginning Meanwhile this is the vigil, second to last before the date April-August 1873

reason: Read verbatim in the Varèse New Directions text, including the leading And and the commas. Dated 1961 because that revised text is the one read; the 1945 wording was not seen. Not shipped, Rimbaud at none of three, not banned, and the line is famous (Neruda closed his Nobel lecture on it).
